title: Simplify the feed decorator
bug: The feed is oldest-first instead of newest-first.

review.why: The PR removes an explicit `order_direction='desc'` argument that matches the decorator's default value, so the feed endpoint continues to return posts in descending timestamp order with no behavior change.

findings.detail: changed: data.*.id x8, data.*.text x7, data.*.url x7, data.*.author.about_me x4, +6 more
findings.label: regression
findings.why: The PR description only mentions dropping default arguments, but the observed change shows different post data (IDs, text, URLs, author details) and timestamps for the same users, indicating a change in feed ordering or content not announced.

suspicions.claim: The feed endpoint now returns posts in ascending timestamp order (oldest first) instead of descending (newest first) because the explicit order_direction='desc' was removed and the decorator defaults to 'asc'.
suspicions.trigger: Authenticate as a user who follows others with posts at different timestamps. Send GET /api/feed with a valid Bearer token. Read the response JSON 'data' array and verify the first post's timestamp is the newest (should be descending). If the first post is the oldest, the order changed.
suspicions.evidence: Multiple GET /api/feed requests show the first post ID changed from high values (151, 145, 143, 90) in base to low values (1, 20, 36) in head, indicating a reversal from descending to ascending timestamp order.
